[Before action · inspect]
Identify all distinct objects, tile boundaries, possible player/avatar, and any UI text or symbols in the initial board.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Board is a 64×64 cell grid (8 px/cell). Initial colors: orange terrain/background; green top boundary; gray bedrock bottom 4 rows; blue 20×4-cell reservoir at cols 12–31, rows 16–19; a black 4×3 plus magenta 4×8 vertical structure near cols 36–39 at top; two yellow W-shaped regions near bottom with six upward prongs total. Progress is 0/6, suggesting the six yellow prongs/targets or six collectibles. Exact controls/mechanics still unconfirmed; test a directional action and compare frames.

[Before action · message]
I expect the black/magenta structure is the controllable object and will shift right by one grid cell; the other colored regions should remain fixed.

[Before action · message]
The black/magenta structure did not move. Instead, the only obvious change is that the top green strip lost its rightmost ~16 pixels, exposing white; progress stayed 0/6 and all underground regions remained fixed. This suggests the strip is a limited action/time meter, so further tests must be purposeful.

[Before action · pixels]
Exactly compare the top meter and the black/magenta structure before and after the right action.

[Before action · message]
I will test direct interaction on the top of the leftmost yellow prong. If yellow regions are the six objectives, it should register 1/6 or visibly alter/select that prong; if interaction instead edits terrain, the changed cells will reveal the tool’s footprint.

[Before action · message]
The click produced no visible board change and no progress; only the green action meter shortened by another two cells. I now expect ACTION5 to be the meaningful activation—likely starting/advancing the black–magenta device or applying the currently selected direction—while the static map itself should otherwise stay unchanged.

[Before action · message]
ACTION5 generated a 22-frame animation but returned the board to the same final layout; the green meter lost two more cells and progress stayed 0/6. The transient frames are therefore essential—I’ll inspect them before spending another action.

[Before action · inspect]
What transient object or wave moves during ACTION5, where does it originate, what path does it take, and why does it fail to score?

[Before action · inspect]
Determine the exact per-frame chronology of all moving/recolored regions during the 22-frame ACTION5 animation, especially the horizontal red/blue block, descending magenta column, yellow targets, gray floor, and any flashes that could encode a required input.

[Before action · inspect]
Determine exact animation chronology, including flashes or directional motion that could encode inputs.

[Before action · pixels]
Measure exact cell geometry/colors of initial and executed horizontal block, vertical source, and bottom targets.

[Before action · message]
The firing animation shows a fixed magenta beam extending downward from the black source; the blue bar merely recolors red, and the bottom floor/targets flash alternately on impact. This now looks like an execution/check phase. I’ll click an empty orange cell directly in the beam’s future path; if clicks place or toggle routing components, a marker should appear there immediately.

[Before action · message]
A strong hypothesis is that arrows set the drill/beam direction while ACTION5 executes it; my earlier right input may have been overwritten by the intervening click. I’ll set LEFT and look for any immediate source change, then—if none—fire immediately to see whether the magenta extension turns left instead of down.

[Before action · message]
LEFT produced no visible preview; only the green meter shortened. I now expect the immediate firing animation either to extend magenta left—confirming a hidden direction setting—or to repeat vertically, ruling that out.

[Before action · message]
The final board again reset with 0/6; I’ll compare one mid-animation frame to the prior firing rather than spend another action.

[Before action · inspect]
Did the immediate LEFT input change the beam/drill path or any animation behavior compared with the prior firing?

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Confirmed board is a 64×64 cell grid (8 px/cell). Orange is the static field. Top row is a green countdown/resource strip that shortens on every play action and leaves white at the right; inspection calls do not change it. Fixed regions: black cols 36–39 rows 1–3; magenta same cols rows 4–7 initially (visual height 32 px); blue horizontal cols 16–35 rows 16–19; two connected yellow W-shaped regions near rows 52–59 with six upward prongs total; gray floor rows 60–63.
ACTION5 is the only control yet producing board animation: over 22 frames the blue region recolors red, the magenta column extends straight down in 4-row increments to the floor, then the gray floor flashes green and yellow regions flash white alternately, and the board resets. It has scored 0/6 twice. LEFT immediately before ACTION5 made the animation exactly identical, so arrows do not set its direction in that phase. ACTION4, ACTION3, and clicks on yellow or orange produced no immediate board change (only countdown loss). Exact objective/control remains unresolved.

[Before action · pixels]
Map the exact yellow geometry to determine whether it represents six separate targets, two cups, letters, or lanes.

[Before action · message]
The yellow regions are exactly two U-shaped cups: each has 32-pixel walls and a 32-pixel opening (left opening x160–191; right opening x352–383). The 32-pixel magenta drop currently falls at x288–319 between them. My previous clicks were either on a cup wall or the current drop lane. I’ll click the center of the left opening near the top; if mouse aiming chooses a drop column, the source should shift to x160–191 or the next firing should use that lane.

[Before action · message]
The source did not visibly shift, so aim may be latent. I’ll fire once: success would show the magenta column at x160–191 entering the left cup and progress increasing; a repeat at x288–319 would rule out direct mouse aiming.

[Before action · message]
Progress stayed 0/6; I’ll verify the beam lane from an archived frame.

[Before action · inspect]
After clicking the left cup opening, did this firing's magenta column move into that lane or remain at x288–319?

[Before action · message]
Mouse aiming is ruled out: the beam remained at x288–319. Since the active object and path are vertical, I’ll test DOWN; unlike the horizontal arrows, it may advance the magenta drill/block one segment or change a vertical state.

[Before action · message]
DOWN, like both horizontal arrows, was blocked/no-op. The magenta 4×4 block is surrounded by orange except for the black 4×3 region directly above, so orange may be impassable and UP is the only locally valid move. I expect UP either to move magenta into the black shaft or register the first objective; if it also no-ops, all directional movement is unsupported.

[Before action · message]
The “no-op” controls reveal a timing mechanic: the green strip’s right edge is a countdown cursor, moving left ~16 px per action. The black/magenta marker spans x288–319; my three firings occurred with the cursor far to its right and all failed identically. The cursor is now at x344. I’ll spend exactly one wait action to move it to ~328, then fire on the following action, which should place it near x312—inside the marker—and register the first of six.

[Before action · message]
The cursor moved exactly to x328 as predicted. Firing now should move it to x312, centered inside the x288–319 timing marker; I expect a visibly different success animation and progress 1/6.

[Before action · message]
The timing hypothesis failed even with the countdown edge inside the marker. One untested direct interaction is the conspicuous blue 20×4 block; ACTION5 always recolors it red at the start, which may be a failure hint identifying the current target. I’ll click its center and expect either progress 1/6 or a persistent color/state change.

[Before action · message]
Clicking blue did nothing, but it advanced the countdown edge to exactly x288—the left boundary of the black timing marker. If scoring requires exact alignment rather than merely overlap, this is the unique moment. I’ll fire now; success should differ immediately or increase progress.

[Before action · message]
The shot did not animate; it caused GAME_OVER as the green edge crossed left of x288. Thus the green strip is a hard deadline/fuse tied to the black marker, not the score target. We have a fresh attempt available; I’ll preserve only the confirmed mechanics and reset.

[Before action · write WORKING.md]
Attempt 1 ended turn14 at 0/6 when an action moved top green fuse from endpoint x288 to x272; ACTION5 then returned GAME_OVER with no animation. Deadline is when green endpoint crosses the black marker's left edge x288, giving ~13 safe actions. Need solve within fresh attempt. Confirmed no-ops: arrows alone and clicks on yellow wall, ordinary orange, left cup lane, or blue. ACTION5 before deadline runs identical 22-frame failure/check animation (blue→red, magenta vertical scan, bottom flashes), scoring 0. Need identify likely rule; all visible geometry/colors documented in GUIDE.

[Before action · message]
I expect RESET to restore the full 64-cell green fuse and the unchanged 0/6 board, giving roughly thirteen actions to execute the correct solution.

[Before action · inspect]
What exact objects move/recolor during ACTION5, and is there any directional branching or target contact? Compare selected animation stages closely.

[Before action · inspect]
What exact objects move/recolor during ACTION5, and is there any directional branching or target contact? Compare selected animation stages.

[Before action · inspect]
Did prior directional or click actions alter any geometry, cell color, or marker around the black source, magenta piece, blue bar, or yellow targets?

[Before action · message]
I expect clicking the blue bar to select/activate it; any selection cue may be subtle, while the fuse should shorten by one cell.

[Before action · message]
Only the top fuse shortened (about 16 px); no selection marker appeared. I now expect Right to move the clicked blue bar toward the magenta drop path if object selection is required.

[Before action · message]
Right produced no geometry change; again only the fuse shortened. This rules out simple click-to-select motion. I will pause actions and decode the fixed pixel pattern and prior execution frames before spending more fuse.

[Before action · inspect]
What exact cell-level glyphs or directional shapes do the yellow regions form, and do they encode a sequence? Enlarge each target cluster and the source/bar junction.

[Before action · message]
No object moved; only another 16 px of fuse vanished. A remaining plausible control is click-to-select plus Space/F to rotate or activate the bar. I expect either a changed blue orientation (supporting that model) or the known straight test animation (falsifying it).

[Before action · message]
The blue-selection test produced the exact known 22-frame failure and no progress; the board reset, with only the fuse shortened. I next expect clicking the magenta emitter block—one of the only untested salient objects—to expose whether it is the actual controllable piece (movement/selection cue or progress); otherwise only the fuse will change.

[Before action · message]
The magenta click caused no cue or progress; only the fuse lost 16 px. I expect clicking the black source/bomb to be the final direct-object test; if inert, mouse interaction is almost certainly not the primary mechanic.

[Before action · message]
The black source was also inert, confirming no direct mouse selection. Before using more actions, I’m comparing the archived shot after the Down–Up–Right input sequence against the baseline to see whether directional inputs alter execution only during animation.

[Before action · inspect]
Does the ACTION5 animation at turn 12 (after Down, Up, Right) differ at any stage or beam coordinate from baseline turn 3? Compare corresponding early, mid, and impact frames.

[Before action · message]
The archived Down–Up–Right shot is pixel-identical to baseline, so directions are likely accumulated commands rather than immediate aiming. The strongest fixed clue is the blue bar’s exact length of six macro-cells extending left; I will test six Left inputs, expecting no immediate geometry change but a queued six-step pattern. First Left should only shorten the fuse.

[Before action · message]
As expected, only the fuse shortened; no board object changed. I expect the second queued Left to behave the same.

[Before action · message]
Again only the fuse shortened. I expect the third Left to add another hidden command with no visible geometry change.

[Before action · message]
Unexpectedly, the blue wire visibly extended left in 32 px macro-cells: by turn 23 its tip reached x≈32. Thus arrows grow a wire from its open tip; Right was blocked because it backtracked into the existing wire. I’m measuring the exact tip positions before choosing a route instead of adding more Left segments.

[Before action · pixels]
At 32-pixel macro-cell centers, where are blue, magenta, yellow, gray, and orange cells on turns 20 through 23, so we can identify the wire tip and each extension?

[Before action · message]
The macro readout confirms the initial wire is cells (x=4…8,y=4); each Left added one cell at the free tip, now (1,4). With this attempt already polluted, I’ll use one Down to confirm that the tip can turn; I expect a new blue cell at (1,5), leaving all other geometry unchanged except the fuse.

[Before action · message]
Down added exactly one blue macro-cell at (1,5), confirming turnable path growth; progress stayed 0 and the fuse shortened. The likely intended route is from the initial tip down, detour around the left yellow U, then contact the gray shared floor in 12 moves, followed by execute. Before resetting, I’ll execute this disposable partial path; I expect every grown blue cell to energize red but still no progress because it reaches neither yellow nor floor.

[Before action · message]
The partial path persisted after execution and returned from red to blue; no progress changed, confirming execution merely tests the drawn path. With too little fuse left to reach a terminal, I’ll extend Down while exhausting this attempt. I expect one new blue cell at (1,6).

[Before action · message]
A new blue cell appeared at (1,6), exactly as expected; only the fuse otherwise changed. I expect another Down to extend to (1,7).

[Before action · message]
The wire extended to (1,7); no other board change beyond the fuse. I expect the next Down to add (1,8), leaving one final action before reset.

[Before action · message]
The wire extended to (1,8), and the green fuse now ends exactly over the black source. I expect the next action to trigger GAME_OVER before applying another cell, enabling a clean reset.

[Before action · message]
Unexpectedly, the 14th Down still applied, extending the wire to (1,9); the fuse passed left of the black source. This shows expiry is enforced when executing, not while drawing. I expect ACTION5 now to produce immediate GAME_OVER without animation, so we can reset cleanly.

[Before action · message]
Unexpectedly, execution after the fuse had passed fully left of the black block animated normally; only exact overlap is lethal. The path remained intact and unscored. I can now finish this disposable route to the shared floor: the next Down should add blue at (1,10).

[Before action · message]
Blue extended to (1,10), with no progress or other change except fuse loss. I expect Down to add (1,11).

[Before action · message]
Blue extended to (1,11); progress remains 0. I expect Down to add (1,12), immediately above the yellow-target row.

[Before action · message]
The wire reached (1,12), with the targets still unchanged. Because x=1 is outside both yellow U-shapes, I expect Down to extend safely to (1,13).

[Before action · message]
Blue extended to (1,13); no target or progress changed. I expect another Down to add (1,14), directly above the gray floor.

[Before action · message]
The tip reached (1,14), immediately adjacent to the gray shared floor; progress is still 0. I expect Down to connect the wire to the floor—possibly leaving gray visually unchanged until execution rather than adding a blue cell.

[Before action · message]
The floor remained gray and progress stayed 0, so the contact is stored without overwriting the target cell (the fuse alone shortened). I expect execution to energize the full blue path into the shared floor and complete all six objectives; if contact was rejected, it will reproduce the failure animation.

[Before action · message]
Execution still ended at 0/6 with the path unchanged, so merely touching the gray floor is not the goal (or the blocked Down never created a connection). I’m inspecting this run’s frame timing to see whether the red signal traversed the grown path or whether arrows simply place barriers.

[Before action · inspect]
During turn 37, how does the grown blue path animate relative to baseline, and does its endpoint ever affect the floor or yellow targets earlier/differently?

[Before action · message]
The animation shows the grown wire only recolors red; it does not transmit along its endpoint. This reveals the actual task: draw a barrier from the free tip around the initial bar and into magenta column x=9, so the descending beam cannot reach the floor/targets. The minimal clean route is Down once, Right five times, then execute (six yellow objectives protected). This attempt’s long path is unsalvageable cheaply. The prior immediate loss followed a blue click then execute, so I’ll use that reset route: clicking blue should arm the same fatal invalid state, with no visible cue besides fuse loss.

[Before action · message]
The click caused no visible change, but the latest full view exposes a major correction: the blue object is still a straight five-cell bar, now translated to (x=1…5,y=11). Arrows move the whole bar; they do not grow a wire. I’m verifying the fresh-position sequence: likely the first Right moved it from x=3…7 to x=4…8, and a second Right would place it across beam column x=9.

[Before action · pixels]
What exact five-cell blue-bar positions occur on the fresh reset and after click/right, and how did Down translate it?

[Before action · message]
The macro samples confirm: fresh bar x=3…7; one Right moves it to x=4…8; repeated arrows translate it rigidly. Thus the clean candidate is two Rights total, placing it at x=5…9 under the magenta beam, then execute. I clicked the current blue bar directly; based on the prior identical sequence, I expect immediate GAME_OVER on execute and then a reset opportunity.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Board is a 16×16 macro-grid (32 px/cell), rendered with 8 px subcell grid lines. Fixed: black source at (9,0), magenta block at (9,1) whose ACTION5 test grows straight down; two yellow U targets at rows 13–14 (x4–6 and x10–12); gray floor row15. The blue controllable piece is a rigid horizontal 5-cell bar, initially x3–7,y4. Arrow actions translate the entire bar one macro-cell (Up/Down/Left/Right); clicks do not move it. Macro-center readouts proved fresh x3–7,y4; one Right gives x4–8; three Left gives x0–4; Down shifts its row. ACTION5 tests placement: blue flashes red, magenta descends, floor flashes green and yellow white on failure, then board placement persists. Clicking the blue bar and immediately ACTION5 causes GAME_OVER and permits RESET. Hypothesis for clean solve: move Right twice so bar x5–9 intersects magenta column x9, then ACTION5; expected to block the descent/protect all 6 objectives. Top green strip shortens per action but is not a simple hard limit; prior exact overlap confused diagnosis.

[Before action · message]
The blue-click test did cause immediate GAME_OVER as expected. I will reset to the initial bar at x=3…7,y=4 and then test the minimal two-Right placement under beam column x=9.

[Before action · message]
I expect the blue five-cell bar to shift one macro-cell right, from columns 3–7 to 4–8, with all fixed objects unchanged.

[Before action · message]
Visible result matches: the blue bar moved right to columns 4–8. The source, magenta block, targets, and floor stayed fixed; the thin top meter changed/shortened slightly. I expect a second right move to put the bar at columns 5–9, directly beneath the magenta source column.

[Before action · message]
The blue bar shifted as expected to columns 5–9; its rightmost cell now intersects the magenta column. Only the top meter otherwise changed. I expect activation to send magenta downward until the blue bar blocks it, protecting both three-cell yellow targets and completing all six objectives.

[Before action · message]
Activation did not complete anything: after a 28-frame animation, the final board returned to the same placement and progress remains 0/6. The overlap hypothesis is therefore false or incomplete. I’ll inspect the animation frames and prior action record before spending another move.

[Before action · inspect]
How do the magenta source, blue bar, yellow targets, floor, and top meter evolve during the failed activation, and where/when does anything collide or flash?

[Before action · message]
The animation reveals the mechanism: liquid hit the bar, spread across it, then ran off just beyond its ends at columns 4 and 10—onto the left walls of the two U-shaped cups—so both targets flashed dark red. Moving the bar one more cell right should make its runoff fall at columns 5 and 11, the two cup openings. I expect the bar to move to columns 6–10 now.

[Before action · message]
The bar moved to columns 6–10 as predicted, aligned so its two runoff streams should enter the cup cavities. The fixed board is unchanged and the top meter shortened. I expect activation to fill both cups and complete all six objectives.

[Before action · message]
Success: activation routed the two streams into the openings, completed level 1, and advanced progress to 1/6. The new board is vertically reversed: source at bottom, three downward-opening cups along the ceiling, two fixed red horizontal deflectors, and a blue movable bar near the middle. I’ll record the confirmed flow rule, then determine the one alignment that feeds all three cups.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Grid puzzle uses 16×16 macro-cells (32 px each; 8 px subgrid). Arrow actions translate the rigid blue horizontal 5-cell bar by one macro-cell; ACTION5 runs the flow; clicks are unnecessary/dangerous. Magenta fluid originates adjacent to a black source and travels away from it. When it strikes a horizontal bar, it spreads across the full bar and continues as two streams one column beyond the bar’s left/right ends. Streams must enter the open cavities of yellow U-shaped cups; striking yellow walls fails. Level 1: source above at x9, cups opened upward with cavities x5,x11, blue initial x3–7,y4. Correct bar x6–10 (Right×3), whose runoff x5,x11 fills cups; ACTION5 advanced to 1/6. Red horizontal bars in later levels appear to be fixed flow deflectors obeying the same split rule. Thin top/bottom green strip is an action budget meter.

Map the exact 16×16 macro-cell occupancy/colors of the new level.

Confirm how the correctly aligned blue bar routed flow into the two cup openings, and identify any visual success cue before the next level appeared.

Click A, then Right×3 to x5–7; x6 splits to x4,x8. B does not intercept. ACTION5 should yield x4,x8,x12.

I expect this first right move to shift the selected bar from 5–9 to 6–10.

[Before action · message]

[Before action · message]
The root bar is now at 7–11 as planned; no other object moved. I expect clicking the upper-left red three-cell bar to select it—turning it blue while the five-cell bar becomes red—without changing positions.

[Before action · message]
Selection behaved exactly as expected: the upper-left three-cell bar is blue, and the other two are red. I expect the first of three right moves to put this bar at columns 3–5.

[Before action · message]
